info.title: Sasai Wallet — Partner API
info.description: Partner-facing external API. Authenticate with X-Sasai-Api-Key plus an HMAC X-Sasai-Signature over the raw request body.

post.description:
Create a user in the API key's tenant, reusing the identity service.

The tenant comes from `principal` (the key), never the body. On a retry
that collides with an existing identifier, returns the existing user (200)
rather than 409 — the identifier is the natural idempotency key.

200.description: Idempotent replay — the user already existed; returned unchanged.

401.description: Missing or invalid API key / signature.

422.description: Validation error — e.g. no email/phone identifier, or a missing Idempotency-Key header.

AccountOut.title: AccountOut
AccountOut.description: Account resource returned from the API.

AddUserToSegmentRequest.title: AddUserToSegmentRequest
AddUserToSegmentRequest.description: Admin payload to assign a user to a segment.

AdjustSystemWalletRequest.title: AdjustSystemWalletRequest
AdjustSystemWalletRequest.description:
Admin fund/withdraw payload for a system wallet.

Positive `amount` = fund (operator deposit). Negative = withdraw
(operator cash-out). `reason` is required for the audit row.

AdminPinResetResponse.title: AdminPinResetResponse
AdminPinResetResponse.description:
Result of an admin-triggered PIN reset.

`delivered_via` is `"sms"` in production (notifications module —
Phase 2). Today it's `"inline"`, meaning the new PIN is included
in the response so the operator can read it back to the user
over a verified channel. NEVER expose this endpoint to non-admins.

ApiKeyCreateRequest.title: ApiKeyCreateRequest
ApiKeyCreateRequest.description: Admin payload to mint a new API key for a tenant.

ApiKeyCreatedOut.title: ApiKeyCreatedOut
ApiKeyCreatedOut.description:
Returned ONCE at creation — carries the plaintext secret. It is never
retrievable again; the operator must copy it now.

ApiKeyOut.title: ApiKeyOut
ApiKeyOut.description: API-key resource as listed — never includes the secret.

AssignRoleRequest.title: AssignRoleRequest
AssignRoleRequest.description: Assign a role to a user.

AuditEntry.title: AuditEntry
AuditEntry.description: Read-side representation of an audit_log row.

AuthStartRequest.title: AuthStartRequest
AuthStartRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /identity/auth/start`.

Mirrors the shape of `OtpSendRequest` (tenant_id + phone) so the mobile
client uses the same input fields across the auth flow. Phone is
normalised here so the lookup compares canonical forms.

AuthStartResponse.title: AuthStartResponse
AuthStartResponse.description:
`POST /auth/start` response — drives the mobile auth branch.

- `needs_otp` → no user exists for (tenant, phone); route through
  OTP → set-PIN registration.
- `needs_pin` → user already exists; route to PIN entry.

BalanceResponse.title: BalanceResponse
BalanceResponse.description:
Available balance for an account.

`available = balance - reserved_balance`. Per Pay-PRD-0130, this is the
figure used for transaction eligibility checks (overdraft prevention).

BonusMultiplierCreateRequest.title: BonusMultiplierCreateRequest
BonusMultiplierCreateRequest.description: Admin create payload — at least one of rule_id/segment_id may be NULL.

BudgetConsumptionOut.title: BudgetConsumptionOut
BudgetConsumptionOut.description: Budget + computed consumption + percent used. Used by the admin UI.

BudgetCreateRequest.title: BudgetCreateRequest
BudgetCreateRequest.description:
Admin payload to create a reward budget.

`scope_id` is required when `scope_type='rule'` (the rule_id); MUST
be null when `scope_type='tenant'`.

BudgetOut.title: BudgetOut
BudgetOut.description: Budget resource returned by the API.

ChangeUserTypeRequest.title: ChangeUserTypeRequest
ChangeUserTypeRequest.description:
Body for PATCH /identity/users/{user_id}/type (Epic 12).

`reason` is mandatory — it is recorded on the audit_log entry so type
changes are traceable (NFR-0250). `parent_user_id` follows the same
Decision D4 compatibility rules as creation.

ConfirmRedemptionRequest.title: ConfirmRedemptionRequest
ConfirmRedemptionRequest.description:
Admin payload simulating provider success callback (Pay-PRD-0690).

Phase F.5 will replace this with HMAC-verified provider callbacks. For
Phase F.4 the endpoint is admin-gated; tenant scopes the lookup.

CreateAccountRequest.title: CreateAccountRequest
CreateAccountRequest.description:
Test-only account creation payload.

Either `user_id` or `merchant_id` is set for user/merchant accounts; both
omitted for system-owned accounts (`system_points_issuance`,
`provider_redemption_wallet`).

CreateRoleRequest.title: CreateRoleRequest
CreateRoleRequest.description: Admin payload for creating a role.

CreateUserRequest.title: CreateUserRequest
CreateUserRequest.description:
Test-only registration payload.

`tenant_id` is accepted in the body because Phase A has no auth.
Production registration (Phase 2) will resolve tenant from the request's
Keycloak realm context.

ExternalCreateUserRequest.title: ExternalCreateUserRequest
ExternalCreateUserRequest.description:
Partner-facing create-user payload.

No `tenant_id` (derived from the API key), and no `user_type` /
`parent_user_id` — the endpoint forces `consumer` with no parent so a
partner can't self-assign a limit/pricing tier or graft the tenant
hierarchy (S7 H1).

ExternalIdentifierIn.title: ExternalIdentifierIn
ExternalIdentifierIn.description:
A partner-supplied identifier — no `verified` flag.

Partners cannot assert that a phone/email is verified; the platform only
marks an identifier verified through its own OTP flow.

FailRedemptionRequest.title: FailRedemptionRequest
FailRedemptionRequest.description:
Admin payload simulating provider failure (Pay-PRD-0700).

Same auth gate as ConfirmRedemptionRequest. Phase F.5 added the real
HMAC-verified provider callback (`/callback`); these `/confirm` and
`/fail` admin endpoints remain as operator overrides.

FeaturedCampaignItem.title: FeaturedCampaignItem
FeaturedCampaignItem.description:
One featured campaign — surfaced fields mapped directly from `Rule`.

Backs the mobile home featured-card slot. Only columns that exist on
the `Rule` model are surfaced; no derived or computed fields beyond
`reward_type` + `reward_value` which together act as the "reward hint"
the card needs to render (e.g. "100 points").

FeaturedCampaignResponse.title: FeaturedCampaignResponse
FeaturedCampaignResponse.description:
Featured-campaign envelope.

Wrapping the item in `{campaign: ...}` lets the empty case stay a
clean 200 with `{"campaign": null}` — the mobile home page collapses
the slot in that case rather than treating it as an error.

FeeQuoteRequest.title: FeeQuoteRequest
FeeQuoteRequest.description:
User-facing request to preview the service charge for ANY service.

Service-agnostic by design: `service` is the service code, which is the
same value as `transaction_type` — the shared lookup key across
pricing_configs, rules, and transactions. Adding a new user service
(cash-in, airtime, redemption, ...) needs no new endpoint; the client
just passes that service's code here.

`account_type` is optional: when omitted it is derived from `currency`
(points instruments settle on the points account, everything else on the
financial wallet), which covers every current service. Pass it explicitly
only to override that default.

FeeQuoteResponse.title: FeeQuoteResponse
FeeQuoteResponse.description:
Computed service charge for one service + amount (no ledger write).

Attributes:
    service: Echoes the requested service code.
    amount: The amount the operation would move (echoes the request).
    fee: Service charge the user would pay on top (Pay-PRD-0260). Zero
        when no pricing config applies to the tuple.
    total: `amount + fee` — what would leave the user's account.
    currency: 3-letter ISO 4217 (uppercase).

FiringOut.title: FiringOut
FiringOut.description: Summary of a single rule firing for the response.

FundUserRequest.title: FundUserRequest
FundUserRequest.description:
Admin top-up payload — credits a user wallet from `system_cash_inflow`.

The user is identified by a registered identifier (phone, email,
account or card) rather than a raw UUID — operators don't have
UUIDs to hand at the counter.

IdentifierIn.title: IdentifierIn
IdentifierIn.description: One identifier provided at registration time.

IdentifierOut.title: IdentifierOut
IdentifierOut.description: An identifier echoed back on responses.

IngestResponse.title: IngestResponse
IngestResponse.description: Result of processing one external event.

InitiateRedemptionRequest.title: InitiateRedemptionRequest
InitiateRedemptionRequest.description:
Redemption initiation payload (Phase F.4 — auth-gated).

`tenant_id` and `user_id` come from the session token via
`get_current_user`. Body carries only the provider + amount.

`pin` is optional — only required when a `step_up_policies` row
for ("redemption", "PTS") sets a threshold below `points_amount`.

code.title: Code
code.description: Uppercase identifier stored in every currency column on the platform. Cannot be changed after creation.

assign_to_existing_users.title: Assign To Existing Users
assign_to_existing_users.description: When true, immediately create one account per existing user for this instrument so they can transact right away.

InstrumentCreateRequest.title: InstrumentCreateRequest
InstrumentCreateRequest.description:
Create payload.

`assign_to_existing_users` controls a one-shot backfill — when true
the service creates one account per existing user in the tenant
(idempotent) so the new instrument is immediately spendable.

InstrumentOut.title: InstrumentOut
InstrumentOut.description: Instrument catalog row returned by the API.

InstrumentUpdateRequest.title: InstrumentUpdateRequest
InstrumentUpdateRequest.description: Patch body — display_name / description / status / symbol.

LimitConfigCreateRequest.title: LimitConfigCreateRequest
LimitConfigCreateRequest.description:
Admin payload for creating a service-wise limit config.

Per-transaction min/max plus rolling count + value caps over
daily/weekly/monthly windows. Every cap is optional but at least one
MUST be set — a row with every field NULL is a no-op config that we
reject at parse time.

LimitConfigOut.title: LimitConfigOut
LimitConfigOut.description: Limit config resource returned by the API.

ManualReviewItem.title: ManualReviewItem
ManualReviewItem.description: One row in the MANUAL_REVIEW queue.

OtpSendResponse.title: OtpSendResponse
OtpSendResponse.description:
`POST /otp/send` response.

`otp` is populated ONLY when the server is configured with
`OTP_DEV_RETURN=true` (local dev only) — see Settings. In production the
field is omitted and SMS gateway delivers the code.

P2PRequest.title: P2PRequest
P2PRequest.description:
P2P transfer payload (Phase F.4 — auth-gated).

`tenant_id` and `sender_user_id` are no longer accepted in the body —
both come from the session token via `get_current_user`. Spoofing the
sender is no longer possible.

`pin` is optional: include it only when a `step_up_policies` row
requires re-verification for the requested amount/currency. The
backend rejects with `step_up_required` if missing when needed; the
mobile client retries with the PIN attached.

P2PResponse.title: P2PResponse
P2PResponse.description:
Result of a successful P2P transfer.

Attributes:
    transaction_id: The double-entry transaction id (Pay-PRD-0170).
    status: Lifecycle state of the transaction ("COMPLETED" on the
        happy path).
    amount: The transferred amount the recipient receives (echoes the
        request).
    fee: Service charge debited from the sender on top of `amount`
        (Pay-PRD-0260). Zero when no pricing config applies.
    total_debited: What actually left the sender's wallet
        (`amount + fee`) — saves the client doing the arithmetic.
    currency: 3-letter ISO 4217 (uppercase) — echoes the request.
    sender_user_id: The authenticated sender (resolved from the
        session token, NOT the request body).
    recipient_user_id: Resolved from the recipient identifier.
    created_at: When the transaction landed (UTC).
    earned_points: Total PTS issued by the rules engine for this
        transfer, or `null` if no rules fired. Surfacing this avoids
        a polling round-trip on the mobile success screen.

PendingItem.title: PendingItem
PendingItem.description: One row in the PENDING redemption list (Pay-PRD-0750).

PointsHistoryItem.title: PointsHistoryItem
PointsHistoryItem.description:
One row in the user's points ledger history (Pay-PRD-0980).

A direct view of `ledger_entries` on the user's points_account, enriched
with the parent transaction's type and (for reward credits) the rule
name that caused the entry.

PointsSummary.title: PointsSummary
PointsSummary.description: Snapshot of a user's points-account state (Pay-PRD-0970).

PricingConfigCreateRequest.title: PricingConfigCreateRequest
PricingConfigCreateRequest.description:
Admin payload to create a fee config.

`fixed_fee + variable_fee_pct` can be zero on either side — but
"zero on both" is the explicit "no-fee" config and is permitted
(operators have to declare it; pricing is never silently skipped).

PricingConfigOut.title: PricingConfigOut
PricingConfigOut.description: Pricing config resource returned by the API.

ProviderOut.title: ProviderOut
ProviderOut.description: Provider resource returned by the API.

ProviderRegistrationRequest.title: ProviderRegistrationRequest
ProviderRegistrationRequest.description:
Admin request to register a redemption provider (Phase F.4 — admin-gated).

Creates the provider row AND the associated provider_redemption_wallet
account (in PTS) atomically. `tenant_id` is in the body because
Keycloak admins span tenants (matches the reconciliation router pattern).

`shared_secret` (Phase F.5) is the HMAC-SHA256 key the provider uses
to sign callback payloads. NULL = provider does not callback; all
transitions must come through the admin operator override endpoints.

RecipientIdentifier.title: RecipientIdentifier
RecipientIdentifier.description: The way the sender refers to the recipient (Pay-PRD-0250).

RedemptionHistoryItem.title: RedemptionHistoryItem
RedemptionHistoryItem.description: One row in the user's redemption history (Pay-PRD-1030).

RedemptionOut.title: RedemptionOut
RedemptionOut.description: Redemption resource returned by the API.

ResolveRequest.title: ResolveRequest
ResolveRequest.description:
Request body for manual resolve.

`outcome=COMPLETED` flips the ledger entries PENDING -> COMPLETED (the
operator vouches the provider actually succeeded).
`outcome=REVERSED` flips PENDING -> REVERSED, restoring the user's points
(the operator vouches the provider failed or the redemption is unsafe).

RoleOut.title: RoleOut
RoleOut.description: Role resource returned by the API.

RuleCreateRequest.title: RuleCreateRequest
RuleCreateRequest.description:
Rule creation payload — Phase C (first_time, milestone) +
Epic 10 expansion (value_based, campaign, streak).

The 3 remaining rule types (composite, referral) still persist OK
but their evaluator branches are deferred to follow-up commits.

RuleOut.title: RuleOut
RuleOut.description: Rule resource returned by the API.

RulePerformanceOut.title: RulePerformanceOut
RulePerformanceOut.description:
Campaign performance metrics for a single rule.

Computed live from `reward_events` — no separate counter table. The
UI surfaces these on the campaigns list and detail drawer.

Fields:
    rule_id: The rule (campaign) these metrics describe.
    total_fires: Count of every issuance for this rule. A user who
        triggered the rule 3 times contributes 3 to this number.
    unique_users_rewarded: DISTINCT user_id count — how many separate
        people have been rewarded at least once.
    total_reward_value: SUM of every reward_value issued. Sum is
        in the rule's reward_type unit (points or cashback currency).
    first_fired_at / last_fired_at: Earliest and latest reward_event
        timestamps. Null when the rule has never fired.
    budget_scope: Which budgets (if any) gate this campaign.
        `none` = uncapped; `tenant_only` = only the tenant-wide cap;
        `rule_only` = only a per-rule cap; `both` = layered (both
        must pass).

RuleUpdateRequest.title: RuleUpdateRequest
RuleUpdateRequest.description:
Partial update — admin can change description, reward_value, status.

Fields that change the rule's TYPE or its trigger conditions are
intentionally not editable: an in-flight `user_rule_progress` row
assumes those values are stable. Operators wanting to change them
should deactivate this rule and create a new one.

SegmentOut.title: SegmentOut
SegmentOut.description: Segment resource returned by the API.

code.title: Code
code.description: Lowercase identifier used in transaction_type fields across the platform. Cannot be changed after creation.

ServiceCreateRequest.title: ServiceCreateRequest
ServiceCreateRequest.description: Create payload — code locked at creation.

ServiceOut.title: ServiceOut
ServiceOut.description: Service catalog row returned by the API.

ServiceUpdateRequest.title: ServiceUpdateRequest
ServiceUpdateRequest.description: Patch body for catalog admin edits.

SourceOut.title: SourceOut
SourceOut.description: A registered source returned by the API.

SourceRegistrationRequest.title: SourceRegistrationRequest
SourceRegistrationRequest.description: Test-only payload to register a new external event source.

StepUpPolicyCreateRequest.title: StepUpPolicyCreateRequest
StepUpPolicyCreateRequest.description: Admin create payload for a new step-up policy.

StepUpPolicyOut.title: StepUpPolicyOut
StepUpPolicyOut.description: Step-up policy resource returned by the API.

SweepRequest.title: SweepRequest
SweepRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /reconciliation/sweep`.

`threshold_minutes` is how long a redemption must have been PENDING before
it's considered stale and eligible for retry. Default 5 — short enough for
test demos, long enough that healthy redemptions aren't disturbed.

SystemWalletOut.title: SystemWalletOut
SystemWalletOut.description: A system-owned account (user_id IS NULL) with its derived balance.

SystemWalletTransactionOut.title: SystemWalletTransactionOut
SystemWalletTransactionOut.description:
A transaction touching a system wallet, surfaced for the drill-down.

`entry_amount` is the amount on the leg that touched this account.
`entry_type` says whether the system account was DEBITed or CREDITed
in this transaction (i.e. did its balance go up or down).

TenantOut.title: TenantOut
TenantOut.description: Tenant resource returned by the API.

name.title: Name
name.description: New display name. Must remain unique across all tenants.

business_type.title: Business Type
business_type.description: Which services are switched on for this tenant.

TenantUpdateRequest.title: TenantUpdateRequest
TenantUpdateRequest.description:
Patch body for tenant identity-card edits.

Both fields are optional — the UI may send just `name` or just
`business_type` depending on which control the operator touched. An
empty body is rejected by the service layer (no-op call indicates a
client bug, not a valid request).

UserAccountOut.title: UserAccountOut
UserAccountOut.description:
Account summary surfaced on the user-detail response.

Includes the derived balance + reserved so the admin UI can render a
full account row without an extra round trip per account.

UserDetailOut.title: UserDetailOut
UserDetailOut.description:
Full user-detail response — admin-only.

Surfaces the data the admin UI needs to render the user drawer:
identifiers, profile, accounts with balances. Transactions /
redemptions arrive via the audit log + reconciliation surfaces.

UserOut.title: UserOut
UserOut.description: User resource returned from the API.

UserProfileIn.title: UserProfileIn
UserProfileIn.description: Optional profile data provided at registration.

WalletLimitConfigCreateRequest.title: WalletLimitConfigCreateRequest
WalletLimitConfigCreateRequest.description:
Admin payload for a per-(tenant, currency) financial-wallet limit config.

A max-balance ceiling plus cumulative send + receive count/value caps over
rolling daily/weekly/monthly windows. Every cap is optional but at least
one MUST be set. Count caps and max_balance must be positive; value caps
non-negative.

WalletLimitConfigOut.title: WalletLimitConfigOut
WalletLimitConfigOut.description: Wallet limit config resource returned by the API.

WalletOut.title: WalletOut
WalletOut.description:
Authenticated user's own wallet — accounts + recent transactions.

Used by the mobile-simulator and the eventual real mobile app. Pure
user-facing: NEVER returns admin-only fields (kyc state, audit ids,
etc). Tenant is implicit — taken from the session token.

WalletTransactionOut.title: WalletTransactionOut
WalletTransactionOut.description:
One transaction row surfaced on /me/wallet — same data the mobile
app shows in its recent-activity feed.

`direction` is derived from the ledger entry on one of the caller's
own accounts: CREDIT → "in" (money/points arrived), DEBIT → "out".
`counterparty_name` is populated for P2P transfers — the other
user's profile first_name — and null otherwise (top-ups, reward
issuance, redemptions where the other side is a system/provider
account with no owning user).

WithdrawFromUserRequest.title: WithdrawFromUserRequest
WithdrawFromUserRequest.description:
Admin withdraw payload — debits a user wallet and credits operator_adjustment.

Identified the same way as fund — by registered identifier, not UUID.
Admin operations are PIN-less and fee-less; operator authentication
is the Keycloak session.
